title: Introduce telemetry-driven onboard pruner and compact release digest
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Motivation: onboarding new models has accumulated a lot of noisy telemetry and ephemeral metadata in profile manifests which inflates changelogs and makes release notes noisy for product engineers. This PR introduces a telemetry-driven 'onboard-pruner' that trims non-actionable telemetry fields and suggests a minimal stable metadata surface for new model versions, plus a 'compact release digest' generator that converts sample diffs and profile deltas into a one-paragraph developer-facing release summary. Design summary: (1) onboard-pruner reads onboarding telemetry (sampling rates, warmup traces, ephemeral config keys) and applies configurable heuristics to identify fields safe to drop from the canonical profile stamp; (2) a compact-digest transformer consumes model-profile deltas and generates prioritized bullet points using heuristics (latency regressions, token-cost deltas, accuracy deltas over baseline prompts) and a short machine-friendly metadata 'skiplist' so automated changelog drafts avoid noise; (3) both components are plumbed into the existing model registry release pipeline as optional pre-merge checks with a gated CLI flag --generate-compact-digest. Implementation notes: the pruner is implemented as a small Go microservice under registry/tools/onboard-pruner and a library function in pkg/profiles/pruner.go. The digest generator is a Python helper in tooling/release_digest/ that emits a compact JSONL and a human-readable blurb; an adapter in registry/ci/ generates draft release notes for the UI. Backwards compatibility: pruning is opt-in for existing manifests via a profile:prune=true field; digest generation defaults to 'draft-only'. Migration: added a migration that tags existing profiles with profile:prune=false to preserve current behavior; a follow-up task (ENG-1822) will run a batch prune for low-signal profiles. Testing and validation: unit tests added for pruning heuristics, e2e runner uses sampled live telemetry from the benchmark-lab fixtures (sanitized). CI: initial lint failure (style/gofmt) fixed in second commit. Rollout: feature gated behind a registry flag and staged rollout to 5% of onboard flows, with fallback to keep full manifests if a regressions threshold is hit. See linked Linear items for rollout schedule and acceptance criteria.

release_notes:
- Add telemetry-driven onboard-pruner (opt-in via profile:prune=true) to reduce noisy metadata in model profiles.
- Add compact release digest generator that produces concise developer-facing release summaries and a machine-readable compact-digest for automation.
- Migration tags existing profiles to prune=false by default to avoid unexpected changes.
- Feature gated and staged rollout; no immediate impact to production unless enabled.
notes_for_ops: Operators: set registry.feature.prune=true to enable for a tenant. The pruner uses a default skiplist which can be extended under /etc/redwood/pruner_skiplist.yaml. If you observe missing required keys, revert per-team config or set profile:prune=false on a model. The digest generator writes drafts to s3://registry-drafts/<model>/<version>.jsonl; ensure lifecycle policy keeps drafts for 30 days.
